headline: Nasdaq futures climb 2% into Black Friday half-session as chip stocks rebound
summary: US stock futures rose sharply ahead of Friday's holiday-shortened session, with Nasdaq-100 futures up about 2%, S&P 500 futures up roughly 1.5% to 1.7% and Dow futures up about 1%, as worries over AI profitability eased and Nvidia gained nearly 4% and Micron about 6% in premarket trading. The 10-year Treasury yield slipped to about 4.84% while Brent crude climbed to around $92 a barrel after Houthi attacks on Saudi energy facilities, ahead of a 1 p.m. ET equity close and a 2 p.m. ET bond close.
why: The move extends Thursday's overseas chip rebound and tests whether this week's AI-led selloff in semiconductors, memory makers and AI infrastructure names has run its course, with retailers also in focus as the NRF expects holiday sales above $1 trillion for the first time. Thin holiday volume can exaggerate moves, and rate-hike worries after hot inflation and growth data plus renewed Middle East supply risk to oil remain unresolved.

headline: Nvidia halts AI server shipments to four Southeast Asian markets as US tightens curbs
summary: Nvidia has asked manufacturing partners to stop shipping servers with its AI chips to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia as Washington tightens export controls, the Financial Times reported, with Dell and Supermicro telling customers there that Nvidia will not authorize their orders. The region matters: Nvidia booked $104 billion of revenue through its Singapore subsidiary in 2025, up 72% from a year earlier, and the step follows new US rules aimed at stopping Chinese firms from renting restricted compute through cloud providers.
why: The report bears on server makers Dell and Super Micro and on Southeast Asian data-center build-outs that have been a fast-growing outlet for AI hardware, and lands as investors already question AI spending. It is unclear whether the suspension is temporary and how quickly operators can secure licenses under the new rules' 90-day window.

headline: SpaceX gains nearly 5% premarket after Musk pledges a share a year to every US child
summary: SpaceX shares rose nearly 5% in premarket trading Friday to about $133.79 after Elon Musk posted on Thanksgiving that he would donate another SpaceX share to every child in America each year, building on Wednesday's plan to give one newly issued Class A share to every active Trump Account, matched personally by Musk. Forbes estimates an annual giveaway at about $8.92 billion based on Wednesday's $127.44 close and nearly 70 million children; the company's contribution transfers in December, while Musk's is due when his lockup ends in June.
why: The pledge keeps retail attention on the recently listed space and AI company and on the Trump Accounts program, which could broaden direct share ownership among households. Key details are unclear, including whether future annual gifts come from new issuance that would dilute existing holders or from Musk's own stake, and how the mechanics would work beyond the first transfer.

headline: China rejects proposed US Section 301 tariffs and reserves the right to retaliate
summary: China's commerce ministry said Thursday it firmly opposes the new Section 301 tariffs Washington proposed on 14 economies, calling the overcapacity probe a breach of WTO rules and saying Beijing reserves the right to take necessary measures; the US plan would put an extra 20% duty on many Chinese goods, lifting the combined rate on some to 45%. Spokesman He Yadong also urged the US to speed up the internal steps needed to activate a $30 billion reciprocal tariff-reduction arrangement agreed in September, whose goods Washington has exempted from the proposal, with US markets closed for Thanksgiving until Friday's shortened session.
why: Beijing's measured wording, with no specific countermeasures named, keeps trade risk in focus for US companies with heavy China sales or supply chains, from consumer electronics and apparel to agricultural exporters. The key open questions are whether China responds before the US-China truce expires on January 10 and how talks at the December G20 summit shape the final duties, which are not due before hearings starting January 25.

headline: Chip stocks rebound overseas and US futures firm as Wall Street shuts for Thanksgiving
summary: With US exchanges closed Thursday, Europe's STOXX 600 rose 1.4% in early trade as its tech sector gained nearly 2%, while in Asia Kioxia jumped 12.6%, SoftBank Group 7.3% and SK Hynix 2.2% and Taiwan's Taiex added 2.5%. S&P 500 futures were up about 0.5% early Thursday New York time after a Wednesday session in which the Nasdaq Composite briefly fell 4.6% before closing down 0.6% and Nvidia lost 3.9% following S&P's warning on its credit rating.
why: The overseas rebound in memory and chip names offers a first read on whether this week's AI hardware selloff in Nvidia, Micron and SanDisk is stabilising, and Reuters tied part of Europe's gain to expectations that proposed US tariffs on the EU will be capped at the agreed 15% rate. Friday's holiday-shortened US session is typically thin, so moves may not prove durable, and Nvidia's governance questions remain unresolved.

headline: FDA pushes Vertex kidney-drug decision to February, sending shares down 7.5% after hours
summary: Vertex said the FDA extended its review of povetacicept for IgA nephropathy by up to three months, moving the target action date from November 30, 2026 to no later than February 28, 2027, after the agency classified Vertex's reply to a late-cycle information request as a major amendment. Vertex said it remains confident in the clinical data and will keep working with the regulator; its shares fell about 7.5% in after-hours trading Wednesday, while rival Vera Therapeutics jumped more than 18%.
why: The delay reshapes the launch race in IgA nephropathy, where Vera Therapeutics is developing a rival treatment and investors are weighing who reaches patients first. The FDA has not publicly said what information it requested, so it remains unclear whether the extension signals a substantive review issue or a procedural one.

headline: S&P puts Nvidia's AA rating on watch for a cut over board oversight after Huang's return
summary: S&P Global Ratings placed Nvidia's AA issuer and senior unsecured ratings on CreditWatch negative, citing weak board oversight of executive conduct, long-tenured directors, no succession plan that leaves the company dependent on Jensen Huang, and questions over internal controls tied to China exposure; it also cut its management and governance assessment to neutral from positive. S&P expects to decide within 90 days and said any downgrade would likely be limited to one notch, and Nvidia shares closed down 3.9% Wednesday after sliding nearly 5% in the afternoon.
why: The action adds a credit-market dimension to the governance questions that have hit Nvidia since Huang's resignation and reinstatement, and Nvidia's swings have been driving the broader AI chip complex including AMD, Micron and Broadcom. Key open items are whether the board announces governance changes and what emerges from Huang's congressional appearances scheduled for early December.

headline: Pharming halts Ruconest production after a failed test, and shares drop 24%
summary: Pharming paused manufacturing of Ruconest, its hereditary angioedema treatment, after a routine manufacturing test failed, notified the FDA and warned that US supply constraints are likely, with current supply expected to last through mid-December. The US-listed shares fell about 17% before the open and closed down 24% on Wednesday.
why: Ruconest is Pharming's core commercial product, so the length of the halt is central to its near-term revenue, and other hereditary angioedema treatment makers could see patients switch if shortages emerge. The company has not said when production will resume or what caused the failed test.

headline: Core PCE climbs to 3.3% and GDP is revised up to 4.3%, locking in December hike bets
summary: The Fed's preferred inflation gauge rose 0.3% in October for a 3.8% annual rate, up from 3.6% in September, while core PCE also rose 0.3% on the month and accelerated to 3.3% from 3.1%; separately, third-quarter GDP growth was revised up to a 4.3% annualized pace from 3.4% and initial jobless claims fell to 189,000. Futures pricing now points to a quarter-point Fed hike at the December 8-9 meeting and another in January, and the data fed a chip-led rout that took the Nasdaq Composite down nearly 4% by late morning before it pared most of the drop in the afternoon as the Dow turned positive.
why: Firm inflation with faster growth strengthens the case for further tightening, which weighs most on long-duration tech and AI names such as Nvidia, AMD, Micron and Broadcom that led Wednesday's slide. It remains unclear how far the Fed will go: Governor Waller has floated a half-point move, and the November jobs and CPI reports still come before the December decision.

headline: USTR proposes Section 301 tariffs on 14 economies, from 15% on the EU to 35% on Vietnam
summary: The US Trade Representative proposed new tariffs on 14 of 16 economies probed for structural excess manufacturing capacity, including up to 20% on China, 15% on the EU, up to 15% on Japan, South Korea and Taiwan, up to 25% on India and up to 35% on Vietnam, with lower rates offered to some partners that conclude trade agreements and no action yet on Mexico and Norway. Comments are due January 5 and hearings start January 25, so final duties are unlikely before late January; the move is widely seen as rebuilding the tariffs lost when the Supreme Court struck down the IEEPA levies in February.
why: Importers and companies with Asian supply chains, from apparel and footwear retailers to electronics makers, face renewed cost uncertainty just as markets digest firmer inflation. Key open questions are how the net-of-existing-duties formula will be calculated, whether goods covered by Section 232 stay exempt, and how the proposal interacts with the US-China truce expiring January 10.

headline: Nutanix beats on Q1 but CEO Ramaswami's exit and a light outlook sink shares 18%
summary: Nutanix's fiscal first-quarter revenue rose 15% to $772.4 million, ahead of the roughly $762.7 million Wall Street expected, and adjusted EPS of $0.73 topped the $0.61 consensus. CEO Rajiv Ramaswami will step down after six years once a successor is found, while the full-year revenue forecast of $3.18-3.23 billion has a midpoint below the $3.22 billion analysts expected; shares fell about 8% after hours and were down nearly 18% in Wednesday's regular session.
why: The reaction shows investors in infrastructure software punishing even clean beats when guidance and leadership are in flux, a read-through for hybrid-cloud peers such as VMware owner Broadcom and Pure Storage. The main uncertainty is who succeeds Ramaswami and whether hardware and memory cost pressure on customers keeps weighing on the outlook.

headline: Ambarella sees Q4 revenue falling about 37% from Q3 as memory shortage hits customers
summary: Ambarella's fiscal third-quarter revenue rose 6.2% to $115.2 million, at the low end of its own $115-124 million guidance, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.28 versus $0.27 a year earlier. The chipmaker forecast fourth-quarter revenue of just $70-75 million, citing a sharp rise in memory prices and scarce supply that is leading customers to cut their outlooks, and the stock fell about 20% in Wednesday's session.
why: The warning is a concrete example of the memory squeeze spilling into edge-AI and consumer device chips, relevant for camera, IoT and automotive suppliers that also lean on DRAM-heavy designs. It is unclear whether the lost revenue is deferred until memory supply normalizes or permanently lost, and how long elevated memory prices will last.

headline: Dell doubles revenue to $54.9 billion, lifts FY27 forecast to $202 billion on AI servers
summary: Dell's fiscal third-quarter revenue rose 103% from a year earlier to a record $54.9 billion, well ahead of the roughly $49.3 billion analysts expected (LSEG), and adjusted EPS of $9.45 beat the $6.59 consensus as AI-optimized server sales jumped 291% to $22.0 billion. Dell raised its full-year revenue forecast to $202 billion from $192 billion, guided next quarter to about $56.3 billion versus $53.6 billion expected, reported a record $132.3 billion AI backlog and added a $25 billion buyback authorization; after an almost 12% slide in Tuesday's regular session, shares swung in extended trading and were last reported up about 4-5%.
why: The order book is a fresh read-through for AI infrastructure demand that informs Nvidia, AMD, Super Micro, HPE and memory suppliers, coming a day after a broad chip selloff. The open question is profitability: AI servers carry thin margins, ISG margin is expected to narrow from 17% toward just under 15% this quarter, PC revenue missed estimates and Dell expects the memory shortage to last into 2027.

headline: Deere guides 2027 profit to $4.5-5.25 billion, below estimates, as large-ag sales sink 15%
summary: Deere earned $1.051 billion, or $3.89 a share, in its fiscal fourth quarter, below the roughly $4.05 analysts expected (secondary source), as total net sales and revenues slipped 2% to $12.1 billion and Production & Precision Ag sales fell 15% with segment profit down to $406 million from $604 million. For fiscal 2027 Deere forecast net income of $4.50-5.25 billion, including a $0.25-0.40 billion one-time pension charge and versus $4.86 billion in 2026, which Reuters reported is below analyst estimates; shares slid in premarket trading.
why: Deere's outlook is a bellwether for the farm economy and for equipment peers such as CNH, AGCO and Caterpillar, with large-ag sales in the US and Canada seen up 5-15% but small ag flat. Uncertainty centres on crop prices and farm incomes, the trade environment after $383 million of tariff recoveries in 2026, and how much of the profit gap reflects the one-off pension charge.

headline: Workday tops on profit and lifts subscription guide, but backlog shortfall hits shares
summary: Workday's fiscal third-quarter subscription revenue grew 12.8% to $2.532 billion and adjusted EPS rose to $2.82 from $2.32, with non-GAAP operating margin widening to 31.4% from 28.5%; total subscription backlog grew a slower 6.1% to $27.5 billion while the 12-month backlog rose 12.3%. It raised full-year subscription revenue guidance to $9.958 billion (13% growth) but guided fourth-quarter subscription growth to 10%, and shares fell about 7% in after-hours trading as backlog came in below estimates, per Dow Jones.
why: Backlog and guidance are a gauge of whether AI is adding to or cannibalising seat-based enterprise software, a debate that also hangs over Salesforce, ServiceNow, Oracle and Intuit. The company says AI products drove nearly $150 million in new annual contract value, but whether that offsets slowing core growth remains to be shown over the next few quarters.

headline: HP beats its own Q4 guide on AI PCs, but memory costs keep FY27 outlook cautious
summary: HP's fiscal fourth-quarter revenue rose 9.3% to $16.0 billion and adjusted EPS of $0.83 cleared its own $0.69-0.79 guidance range, helped by a $0.15 tariff-refund benefit, as commercial PC revenue climbed 23% even though Personal Systems margin fell to 3.0% from 5.8%. HP guided fiscal 2027 adjusted EPS to $3.15-3.45 and free cash flow to $2.9-3.1 billion, below 2026's $3.33 billion, citing ongoing memory and storage cost pressure, and raised its quarterly dividend to $0.31; shares jumped as much as roughly 9% after hours before giving back part of the gain.
why: The results show how the memory price surge is squeezing PC makers, a read-through for Dell's PC unit, Lenovo and component buyer pricing power. The new EPS range also switches to excluding stock-based compensation from fiscal 2027, so comparisons with prior years and consensus need care.

headline: Brokers race to let AI agents trade for clients: Interactive Brokers, Robinhood and eToro all go live
summary: Interactive Brokers launched IBKR Autonomous Trading on 21 October 2026: eligible clients can authorise a connected AI to scan more than 75,000 listed stocks, options and ETFs and submit supported orders without approving each one, inside a separate 'AI Partition' funded from their main account. Robinhood rolled out non-technical AI trading agents to its roughly 29 million users at its HOOD Summit on 29 September, and eToro launched connectors for Claude, ChatGPT and Grok on 8 October; in its 10 November Q3 results eToro said users engaged in API and agentic trading rose 250% from Q2 (secondary source).
why: Agent trading could lift trading volumes and client activity — the main revenue drivers for IBKR, HOOD and ETOR — but liability for agent mistakes is still unsettled and FINRA has flagged autonomous agents as needing new supervision. All three firms ring-fence the agent in a separate sub-account with its own funding limit, which caps losses but not the risk of a bad strategy.

sources.name: Interactive Brokers press release (Business Wire via Nasdaq), 21 Oct 2026

headline: Analog Devices beats on 42% growth, yet shares sink ~17% on softer guide and capex jump
summary: Analog Devices posted record fiscal Q4 revenue of $4.37 billion, up 42% from a year earlier and ahead of the roughly $4.32 billion consensus, with adjusted EPS of $4.06 versus about $3.89 expected and up 80% year on year. It guided fiscal Q1 revenue to $4.4 billion ±$150 million but adjusted EPS to $3.82 ±$0.20, below the quarter just reported, and lifted fiscal 2027 capex to $1.6–1.9 billion from $0.7 billion; shares fell about 17–18% premarket and were down roughly 19% by midday.
why: The reaction is a read-through for analog and mixed-signal peers such as Texas Instruments, Microchip and NXP, where investors are weighing strong industrial and data-center demand against heavier spending and easing gross margins. Management said bookings still run above billings, so the open question is whether the capex build and the guided dip to about 74% gross margin prove temporary.

headline: Chipmakers give back Monday's surge as Nvidia drops 7–9% and Nasdaq slides about 2%
summary: A day after Nvidia jumped about 31% on Jensen Huang's reinstatement as CEO, the stock fell roughly 7–9% intraday Tuesday, AMD lost about 9%, Micron and SK Hynix dropped more than 10% and SanDisk, Seagate and Western Digital each fell 5% or more. The Nasdaq Composite was down about 1.5–2% through the session while the Dow rose roughly 0.6–0.8% as money rotated into healthcare and retailers, with the 10-year Treasury yield near 4.9%.
why: The swing shows how crowded the AI hardware trade has become, with memory, storage and GPU names moving together on sentiment rather than company news. Wednesday's PCE inflation report and traders' high odds of another Fed rate hike remain the next tests for richly valued tech stocks.

headline: Dick's jumps ~16% as Q3 profit tops forecasts and full-year EPS outlook moves higher
summary: Dick's Sporting Goods reported Q3 net sales up 23% to $5.13 billion, helped by a full quarter of Foot Locker, and adjusted EPS of $1.94 against a consensus near $1.41, with comparable sales up 2.6% at the core Dick's business and 0.5% at Foot Locker. It raised its 2026 adjusted EPS outlook to $11.45–$12.30 from $11.00–$12.00, bought back $903 million of stock in the quarter, and its shares rose about 16% Tuesday morning.
why: The results inform the read on athletic retail and brand partners such as Nike, as Foot Locker posts its first slight comp gain under new ownership. Foot Locker remains loss-making, with 134 stores closed so far this year and up to $750 million in total restructuring charges planned.

headline: Best Buy posts its strongest comps in five years at +6.1% and lifts full-year outlook
summary: Best Buy's fiscal Q3 revenue rose 5.8% to $10.24 billion and comparable sales grew 6.1%, well above the roughly 2.3% analysts expected, while adjusted EPS of $1.62 beat the $1.49 consensus and rose from $1.40 a year earlier. The retailer raised fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to $43.0–$43.3 billion and adjusted EPS to $6.90–$7.05 from $6.70–$6.90, and its shares rose about 5% before the open.
why: Gains in computing, mobile and services point to a hardware upgrade cycle that matters for suppliers such as Apple and HP heading into the holidays. Q4 comp guidance of 2–4% is more modest, and domestic margins were helped by $41 million of one-off tariff refunds.

headline: Kohl's returns to sales growth and tops EPS forecasts, helped by one-time gains
summary: Kohl's reported Q3 comparable sales up 1.2%, its first positive quarterly comp in a long stretch of declines, and adjusted EPS of $1.76 against Wall Street expectations near breakeven, with gross margin up 145 basis points to 41.0%. It raised its 2026 outlook to diluted EPS of $4.30–$4.50 and flat to +0.5% sales, and shares rose about 13% premarket and roughly 17% by midday.
why: A turn at Kohl's adds to evidence that middle-income shoppers are holding up for department stores such as Macy's heading into the holidays. Tariff refunds, a real estate gain and a tax benefit inflate both results and guidance, and management expects a more promotional fourth quarter.

headline: Sanofi bets $41 billion on Insmed, paying a 46% premium in all-cash biotech deal
summary: Sanofi agreed to buy Insmed for $175 per share in cash, valuing the drugmaker at about $41.0 billion and paying roughly 46% above its Nov. 18 close, the last price before deal reports surfaced. Sanofi will fund the purchase with debt and cash, expects it to add to business EPS by the end of 2028, and leaves its 2026 guidance unchanged; Insmed shares rose about 14% before Tuesday's open.
why: The deal shows big pharma paying up for late-stage growth as blockbusters such as Sanofi's Dupixent approach patent expiry, which keeps attention on other mid-cap biotechs. Closing, targeted for the first half of 2027, still needs Insmed shareholder approval and US and international antitrust clearance.

headline: HPE beats and raises, yet shares slide as AI server boom threatens margins
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise grew fiscal Q4 revenue 50% to $14.5 billion, earned $1.43 a share on a non-GAAP basis against its own $1.20-$1.30 forecast, lifted its fiscal 2027 outlook to $5.05-$5.35 per share and added $5 billion to its buyback. Shares still fell roughly 10% to 12% before Tuesday's open after management said its Cloud & AI segment margin could ease to about 14% next year from 18.4% in Q4 as lower-margin AI systems make up more of sales.
why: The reaction puts AI hardware profitability, not just demand, under the spotlight, a question that also hangs over server peers such as Dell and Super Micro. How deep the squeeze runs depends on the timing and mix of AI system shipments, which HPE expects to tilt toward the second half of fiscal 2027.

headline: Dollar Tree shoppers keep coming: traffic-led Q3 beat lifts full-year outlook
summary: Dollar Tree's Q3 comparable sales rose 4.6% as store visits climbed 3.8%, lifting net sales 6.9% to $5.07 billion, and adjusted EPS of $1.16 cleared the $0.91 consensus despite a $0.42 hit from tariff-related reinvestment. The retailer raised its full-year adjusted EPS outlook to $8.05-$8.25, including about $0.65 from tariff refunds, and shares jumped about 11% in premarket trading.
why: Rising traffic at a discount chain is an early read on how budget-conscious households are spending into the holiday season, relevant for peers like Dollar General and Five Below. Part of the higher outlook rests on one-time tariff refunds, so the underlying earnings trend is less clear than the headline raise suggests.

headline: Agilent tops estimates with a 30% operating margin, sending shares higher premarket
summary: Agilent's fiscal Q4 revenue reached $2.04 billion against a $1.99 billion consensus, and adjusted EPS of $1.86 beat the $1.73 estimate. Adjusted operating margin widened 280 basis points to 30%, and shares rose about 5.7% before Tuesday's open.
why: Agilent is a bellwether for lab-instrument and life-science tools spending by drugmakers and research labs, so its results are watched across the sector. Whether the early gain holds is uncertain on a day when tech-heavy futures were pointing lower.

headline: US stocks rebound sharply as chip and AI shares lead after last week's rout
summary: By midday Monday the Nasdaq Composite was up about 6.7% and the S&P 500 about 4.9%, with the Philadelphia chip index up roughly 13% and every sector but energy higher. The bounce follows a week in which the S&P 500 fell 8.6% and confirmed a correction.
why: A broad rebound eases pressure on tech-heavy portfolios, but futures pricing still points to a likely Fed rate hike in December and October PCE inflation data is due Wednesday.

headline: Tesla jumps about 12% on SpaceX merger reports, HSBC upgrade and market rebound
summary: Tesla rose as much as 13.9% on Monday as Bloomberg reported a possible Tesla-SpaceX merger could come as soon as December, and HSBC raised the stock to hold from reduce with a $359 target, up from $157. The move came during a broad tech rally and after the weekend rollout of FSD version 15.
why: A combination with SpaceX would reshape Tesla's valuation and shareholder base, but no merger has been officially announced and terms, timing and approvals are unknown.

headline: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO; shares jump about 30%
summary: Nvidia's board brought co-founder Jensen Huang back as president, CEO and director with immediate effect, 11 days after he resigned. The stock opened up about 33%, its largest intraday gain since 2003, and lifted chipmakers and AI-infrastructure names including neocloud providers.
why: Removes the leadership uncertainty behind November's AI selloff. An SEC inquiry, shareholder lawsuits and national-security questions remain open.

headline: Arm extends CEO Rene Haas's contract through 2033; shares climb about 16%
summary: Arm said Rene Haas will keep leading the chip designer through 2033 and will also become vice chairman of majority owner SoftBank Group from December 1. Earlier this month Nvidia's board had reportedly approached Haas as a possible successor to Jensen Huang.
why: The extension settles leadership questions at Arm and ties Haas more closely to SoftBank. How his larger SoftBank role will split his time is not yet clear.

headline: CrowdStrike agrees to buy Zscaler in all-stock deal worth about $43.9 billion
summary: CrowdStrike will pay 1.135 of its shares for each Zscaler share, about a 34% premium to Zscaler's previous close. Zscaler rose sharply before the open while CrowdStrike fell about 9%, as investors weighed dilution for the buyer.
why: Creates one of the largest pure-play cybersecurity companies and a stronger rival to Palo Alto Networks. The deal still needs shareholder and regulatory approval.
